open_points.subject: JSON-depth validation at kernel entry boundaries
open_points.text: “A deeper text is a value JCS cannot represent, refused where it enters as A01 rule 1 says” conflicts with `data_provider`’s “Must not own … any check that uses a ceiling”, while `canonical_values` owns refusal of values JCS cannot represent and `installation`—which must reject an over-depth configuration before parsing—may know only `models`, `data_provider`.
open_points.question: Which module owns the non-recursive `json_depth` measurement and refusal mechanism, and how may `installation` use it without violating its declared dependencies?
options: `canonical_values` owns a reusable raw-JSON depth scanner and `installation` may know it
Each entry-owning module implements the measurement independently
`data_provider` owns executable validation despite its stated prohibition
open_points.default_guess: `canonical_values` owns the scanner, and `installation` is allowed to depend on it.

open_points.subject: Function-output byte counting when canonicalization fails
open_points.text: “The output count is the sum of the canonical JSON bytes of every `value` output — for an output that has none, the bytes of its JSON text as returned” is not allocated between `sandbox_runner`, which “pre-counts the outputs and sends them”, and `sandbox`, which owns “the output count kept from outside”; a Python `run` returns objects, so no module is said to create or expose the fallback JSON text.
open_points.question: Which module creates the exact fallback JSON text, and what trusted artifact does `sandbox` receive so it can enforce `output_bytes` before classifying the output as a contract violation?
options: `sandbox_runner` serializes each output and reports framed bytes that `sandbox` counts
`sandbox` serializes the decoded runner result itself
The runner sends raw per-output JSON text and `sandbox` validates and counts it
open_points.default_guess: The runner sends raw per-output JSON text, while `sandbox` performs the authoritative byte count and classification.

open_points.subject: Depth failure of an assembled mapped list
open_points.text: A13 now says a list “which nests deeper than `json_depth_max` … is not written”, but `run_values` owns only “measuring every delivered list … against `stored_value_bytes_max`”, while `run_graph` must not own “the size measure of a list (`run_values`)” and `data_provider` must not own checks that use a ceiling.
open_points.question: Which module measures an assembled mapped list’s depth and returns the over-depth result from which the node failure is derived?
options: `run_values.assemble_mapped_lists` checks both byte size and depth
open_points.default_guess: `run_values` invokes `canonical_values` and reports either byte-size or depth overflow to `run_graph`/`runs`.
